review: 1:4 כְּזָר וּכְנָכְרִי — 'like a stranger and a foreigner', for مِثْلَ إِنْسَانٍ غَرِيب; the doublet is a Hebrew idiom (Exod 12:43, Isa 61:5).
1:7 וַיַּעֲטִירוּהוּ קוֹצִים — qal of עטר with a thorn-crown object; the alternative הִכְתִּירוּהוּ is post-biblical.
2:2 בְּכֶבֶל — 'with a chain', biblical (Ps 105:18 עִנּוּ בַכֶּבֶל); the Arabic الْقُيُود is plural, Hebrew uses the collective singular.
3:3 יָנִיעוּ רֹאשׁ — the exact mocking gesture of Ps 22:8 and Matt 27:39, so the Hebrew quotes the psalm rather than translating يُنْغِضُونَ الرَّأْس.
3:5 וּבַחֲנִית דְּקָרוּהוּ — 'and with a spear they pierced Him', the Johannine piercing (John 19:37, Zech 12:10); דָּקַר is the verb of Zech 12:10.
4:3 חֶרֶב הַצֶּדֶק — 'the sword of justice', for سَيْفُ الْعَدْل; צֶדֶק is chosen over מִשְׁפָּט because the line needs the shorter word.
